blocks.0: Vav Hebrew Letter (ו): Sound, Vowels & Practice

1.tip: Holam Male represents the [o] sound, similar to the [o] in the English word 'no.'

3.content: The letter Bet (ב) at the end of a word is usually pronounced as [v], like in the English word 'vase.'

5.tip: Shuruk (וּ) is a vowel mark that produces the [u] sound, similar to the English word 'moon.'

7.content: How do you pronounce the Hebrew word for 'hook' (וַו)?
7.tip: The Hebrew word 'וַו' (vav) consists of two Vav letters. The first Vav has a Patach (ַ), producing the [va] sound, while the second Vav is pronounced [v].

8.tip: Patah represents the [a] sound. When combined with Vav (וַ), it produces [va].

theory.heading: Meet Vav
theory.intro: The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Vav usually makes a [v] sound, and can also work as a vowel letter for [o] or [u].
objectives: Hear its [v] sound, and the two vowel marks used only with Vav: Holam Male [o] and Shuruk [u].
Read Vav in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">דוֹב</bdi> (bear).

examples.heading: Holam Male, Shuruk and new words
examples.intro: Meet two vowel marks that appear only with Vav — Holam Male [o] and Shuruk [u] — then see Vav in real Hebrew words.
